competency_fulfillment.rationale: Competency requires comparing 1/2 and 1/4 using models, but none of the 5 samples ask a comparison between the two fractions; three ask students to name what fraction '1/2 equal parts' represents, and two ('Which is greater: 10 or 6?') compare whole numbers with no fraction or model in sight.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: fractions registers 3 axes/9 combos and comparing_ordering registers 3 axes/8 combos per variant_registry; validate_matrix machine-verifies exhaustive execution of that combo space, and these 5 seeds are only an illustrative slice of it.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Both observed question types are single, direct sentences well under the 15-word grade-1 cap ('What fraction does 1/2 equal parts represent?' is 8 words), appropriate single-step recall for grade 1 quarter 4.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The comparing_ordering axis appears to drive plain integer comparisons (10 vs 6, 18 vs 30) rather than fraction-vs-fraction comparisons, so the registered variant space as sampled does not obviously exercise the 1/2-vs-1/4 model comparison this competency names.

competency_alignment.rationale: None of the sampled content reaches beyond grade-1 scope, but the fraction item tests bare identification of 1/2 rather than the comparative judgment (which is bigger, half or a quarter) the competency wording specifically demands.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The whole-number magnitudes seen (6-30) and the single denominator pair (halves, quarters) are both well within an early grade-1 range, so scale itself is not the issue for this node.
